title: Protected Trust
paragraphs: “Huh? Huh? Huh?”
Father stared at us in blank confusion.
“Well, it’s only natural that you’d be surprised. I didn’t believe it myself until Motoyasu showed me the proof.”
“Yeah, I nearly got played for a fool, too.”
Ren and Itsuki gave Father friendly smiles as they spoke. At last… we had saved him.
“W-What exactly is going on…?”
Father looked at me, bewildered. Of course, he had no idea what was happening.
“We can explain everything in detail later, but for now… just know this, Father: we believe that you are innocent.”
“…Father?”
“Motoyasu insists on calling Naofumi that for a certain reason. We’ll explain it later, so just ignore it for now.”
“I personally don’t get it either, but since Motoyasu has taught me so much, I can’t really tell him off for it.”
“Haa…”
Father tilted his head, still not quite grasping the situation. But gradually… his eyes welled up with tears.
“You all… you really believe I didn’t do it?”
“Of course.”
“Yes. Naofumi-san is absolutely innocent.”
“That’s right. There’s no way Father would do something so disgraceful!”

His tears overflowed faster than he could wipe them away, leaving his face a mess. He sniffled. I could feel how much it meant to him to be believed. Even Ren and Itsuki, a little embarrassed, blushed at his reaction.
“B-Bububu! Bubuhibububu!?”

The Crimson Swine let out a hysterical squeal, fake crying while screeching at us. Stay away! Now that we had secured Father’s trust—along with Ren and Itsuki’s—you had no more value. If you want to live even a second longer, you’d best start running. Not that you’d last more than a few seconds.
“Shut up. We’re not falling for your lies.”
“Thinking about how I might have believed you if Motoyasu hadn’t told me the truth sends chills down my spine.”
“They say beautiful flowers can be poisonous… but this is lethal venom. Worse, she smiles as she watches people suffer.”

With sharp glares, Ren and Itsuki readied their weapons, shifting into battle stances. Hmm… even if they are Heroes, it’s dangerous for them to fight right now. Especially Itsuki—he’s only level 1 because of my, uh… tracking methods. And Father should still be at level 1 as well.

“Amaki-dono, Kawasumi-dono, Kitamura-dono, what in the world are you doing? That Shield Hero attempted to violate his comrade, yet you would defend him? Even if you are fellow otherworlders, there are some things that simply cannot be excused!”

Trash was desperately trying to steer things back to his desired outcome. But it was too late. Ren and Itsuki knew the truth. Now, everything that came out of Trash and the Crimson Swine’s mouths would only look like attempts to drag them into a crime.
“Hmph. You talk as if we know nothing, but we do. We know that this country sees the Shield Hero as an enemy of its religion.”
“An enemy of religion!?”
Father let out a gasp of surprise upon hearing the reason. Ren was absolutely right. For the crime of shamelessly insulting Father as they pleased, they must pay with their own bodies.

“If they had secretly killed Father immediately after summoning him, we would have become suspicious. And considering his status as a Hero, such an act would have drawn the ire of foreign nations—there would be no avoiding it.”
“Exactly. That’s why they framed Naofumi-san as a criminal, turned us against him, and then planned to have us kill him when the opportunity arose.”
“And if Father had tried to flee to another country before we became strong, they would have killed him quietly before word could reach us.”
The countless loops had already made that clear. I had seen it all firsthand—there was no mistake.
“Enough of this farce. We refuse to be your puppets any longer.”
“That’s right. We’re leaving this country immediately. We’ll find another—a place that treats all Heroes equally.”
“We are Heroes. We will not be controlled by selfish, lazy parasites like you.”
Stepping forward, I raised my spear, positioning myself to shield Father. Ren and Itsuki followed suit, brandishing their weapons to keep the surrounding soldiers in check.
“Bow your heads and beg for forgiveness. If I feel merciful, I might just spare your lives.”
Though honestly, that would never happen. Not even if the world turned upside down.
“Buhii!”
The Crimson Swine abruptly stopped fake crying and spat something out. Its true colors had finally shown.
“Guh…!”
Trash let out a frustrated groan. Now then… will they actually let us go?
“If you had just obeyed, all would have been fine… but enough!”
Trash stood up and declared loudly:
“Men! Kill these false Heroes at once!”
“Buhii! Buhibuhii!”
The Crimson Swine squealed something, no doubt adding some sadistic detail—like severing our limbs before finishing us off.
“No matter. We will simply perform another Hero Summoning Ceremony. This time, we shall call forth true Heroes!”
Did they really think they could defeat us?
Did they seriously believe they could win against Heroes? The sheer absurdity of it nearly made me laugh.
“If it’s an order, then we have no choice.”
With that, Ren and Itsuki’s former comrades drew their weapons against us. Ren and Itsuki’s expressions twisted with unease. More soldiers arrived, one after another, surrounding us.
“We had such a long talk just yesterday, and yet…”
“It can’t be helped. They’re in on it too.”
“They tried to deceive us, thinking we were just some naïve Otherworlders. And when that failed, they labeled us as fakes and decided to slaughter us all. Unbelievable.”
However, Ren and Itsuki were visibly breaking into a cold sweat. Well, that’s only natural. Their levels were still in the single digits.
“Ren, Itsuki, Father—step back. At your current strength, even a single soldier would be a tough fight for you.”

Thanks to the Hero’s weapons, they were stronger than the average person. But still, level mattered in this world. If this were a game, enemies in early story events would be balanced accordingly. But this was not a game. Even for Ren and Itsuki, taking an attack from a high-level soldier and remaining standing seemed unlikely.
…Though now that I think about it, I recall Father stopping a soldier’s punch at this stage.
Was the soldier just low-level? Or was Father’s defense absurdly high even from the start? Come to think of it, Father once mentioned that he didn’t even understand how to strengthen his own Shield.

Could it be that he had been unconsciously activating some kind of enhancement all along? If I had to guess… it might be similar to what happened when Fiancée was kidnapped. Or rather, when I lost my combat ability. From that moment, up until Itsuki went berserk, I felt like my attack power had dropped slightly. It wasn’t enough to concern me at the time, especially since I had already started sharing enhancement methods. But now that I think about it, I did notice a small decline. And then, at some point, it simply returned to normal.
I had dismissed it as my imagination back then… but was it? Another thing—there are many enhancement methods, but none of them explicitly mention sharing enhancements.

We’ve always treated it as common knowledge, but what if that was the Shield’s true enhancement ability? The thought suddenly crossed my mind. But now wasn’t the time to dwell on that. Right now, the priority was breaking out of this situation. Though, to be honest, wiping out this lot would be easier than twisting off a baby’s wrist. At this moment, I recalled something Father had once said.
“Even if you crush the head, another one will sprout immediately. Nothing will change.”
But by this point… things would change. I had been shocked when killing Smoked Meat hadn’t altered the outcome before. But if I killed Trash here…
Well, I was curious to see what would come crawling out next.
“If you kill the Shield with your own hands, we may let you live.”
“Shut up! I’d rather die here than let myself be used by the likes of you!”
“I agree with Ren-san. The world is on the brink of destruction, and yet you people waste time discriminating against others. I refuse to fight for people like you.”
“Then let’s go. You fools will understand—with your very lives—just how foolish it is to oppose a Hero!”
“Ren, Itsuki, Motoyasu… thank you.”
Such gracious words. Just hearing them filled me with strength, many times over.
